dedupe_keys.name: green roofs in basel switzerland combining mitigation and adaptation

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes how Basel, Switzerland, reached the world's largest green roof area per inhabitant, 5.71 square metres in 2019, through two time-limited subsidy programmes (1996-1997 at up to 20 CHF per square metre, and 2005-2007 at 30 to 40 CHF for retrofits) paid from an Energy Saving Fund fed by 5 percent of electricity bills, followed by building regulations that require green roofs on suitable flat roofs. The drive began with energy saving and biodiversity, promoted by researchers of the Zurich University of Applied Sciences with the city's environment and energy department, business, horticulture and nature associations; green roof costs have since fallen from about 100 to 23 CHF per square metre, and subsidies are no longer needed. Coverage is the city of Basel, with CH2018 projections of hot days rising from 10.5 to 68.5 a year by 2085 under RCP8.5. The page, published in 2016 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal. Caveats: adaptation benefits such as runoff reduction and indoor cooling are expected, not measured, and results rely on a local champion. It illustrates climate adaptation of buildings through green infrastructure against heat and flood hazards; related records are the Hamburg Green Roof Strategy and Berlin Biotope Area Factor case studies.
name: Green roofs in Basel, Switzerland (combining mitigation and adaptation)
organisations: City of Basel Department of Environment and Energy
outcomes: Basel reached 5.71 m2 of green roof per inhabitant in 2019, the highest per capita worldwide, and green roof costs fell to about 23 CHF per m2 so subsidies were ended.
provider: Climate-ADAPT (European Environment Agency), case study from ZHAW Wädenswil and the GRaBS project
resources_used: Basel Energy Saving Fund incentive programmes
